title: Immunohistochemistry Protocol
author: Kristin Anderson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sppedmn

steps.title: Gross specimen and load processor
steps.instruction: Gross one specimen at a time at the Mopec grossing station, verify cassette ID against specimen container, dispose contaminated biohazard bags in approved containers, load the cassette‑holding rack into the Sakura Tissue‑Tek VIP6 AI and select Program 8 for processing.

steps.title: Run Tissue‑Tek Program 8
steps.instruction: Execute Program 8 in the processor with the following reagent sequence and times:

steps.title: Prepare embedding station
steps.instruction: Ensure the Tissue‑Tek TEC embedding station paraffin reservoir is full; if not, fill it with molten paraffin from the TBS Liquid Paraffin Dispenser before the processor finishes.

steps.title: Embed tissue in paraffin blocks
steps.instruction: Transfer processed samples from the VIP6 AI to the warming reservoir of the embedding station, embed immediately to prevent RNA degradation, and embed one cassette at a time using a square‑base mold.

substeps.instruction: Fill the mold with molten paraffin from the dispenser.
Remove the cassette lid, lift the specimen with forceps, orient the tissue on its edge flush against the bottom of the mold.
Place the cassette on top of the mold, top off with additional molten paraffin, then move the cassette to the cooling plate.

steps.title: Trim paraffin blocks
steps.instruction: Trim the resulting FFPE blocks with the Wax Trimmer to expose tissue for sectioning.

steps.title: Prepare microtome and cool blocks
steps.instruction: Set up the microtome water bath and pre‑cool the blocks before cutting.

substeps.instruction: Turn the water bath on, fill with distilled water, and set the heating element to 37 °C.
Remove the Histocool block from the freezer, fill it with distilled water, and wait 10–15 min before placing blocks on it.
Match each FFPE block with its RFS form and slides to confirm identifiers.
Place blocks tissue‑side down on the Histocool block; pre‑cooling is required for quality sections.
Allow blocks to soak on ice for approximately 20 min (time may vary with fixation).

steps.title: Section tissue and collect slides
steps.instruction: Cut sections on the microtome and mount them on slides.

substeps.instruction: Face each block to obtain a full tissue section.
Replace the microtome blade as needed to avoid cutting artifacts.
Lay the ribbons onto the water bath and pick up sections onto the corresponding slides.
Remove the FFPE blocks from the Histocool block, pat dry any excess water, and place the blocks in a plastic bag for return to the investigator.
If a cassette contains no tissue or shows embedding problems, annotate the specimen ID on the RFS requisition form.

steps.title: Dry sections before staining
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the slides overnight, then oven‑dry them.

substeps.instruction: Place slides in a slide‑drying rack and allow them to air‑dry overnight.
Dry the paraffin sections at 60 °C for 1 hour.
Remove the slides from the oven and let them cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Load slides into H&E stainer
steps.instruction: Place the dried slides into the Sakura DRS2000 for H&E staining.

substeps.instruction: Load slides into the black H&E slide‑staining rack(s) and attach the rack to the plastic staining arm.
Open the DRS2000 by gently pushing the bottom door, insert the staining arm with rack(s) into the S1/S2 loading station, and close the door.
Press F1 [START]; verify that the method displayed reads “F FPE H&E”.
If the method is incorrect, press F2 [METHOD] and use the up/down buttons to select the correct “F FPE H&E” protocol.
Press F1 [START] to begin the staining run.

steps.title: Run FFPE H&E staining program
steps.instruction: Execute the FFPE H&E program with the following reagent sequence and times:

steps.title: Post‑stain handling
steps.instruction: Remove slides from the stainer and prepare for coverslipping.

substeps.instruction: When the program finishes (beep), press F1 [REMOVE], open the door, and carefully remove the E1/E2 Xylene bucket (Program End); carry it to the coverslipping area.
Transfer the slide racks to one of the Xylene buckets at the coverslipping area.
Place the Xylene bucket back into the Program End station, close the stainer door, and press F1 [CONFIRM].

steps.title: Coverslip H&E slides and QC
steps.instruction: Mount the stained sections and complete quality control.

substeps.instruction: Coverslip the slides using Cytoseal XYL and a VWR 24 × 40 coverglass.
Wipe the back of each slide and drain the sides to remove excess mounting media/xylene, then place the slides on a cardboard palette to dry overnight.
Fill out the H&E QC sheet and place the slides together with the sheet in the QC bin for Director/Operations Manager approval.

steps.title: Dehydrate and clear IHC slides
steps.instruction: Run the IHC dehydration/clearing sequence on the slides.

substeps.instruction: Three changes of 95 % Ethanol, 1 min each.
Three changes of 100 % Ethanol, 1 min each.
Five changes of Xylene, 1 min each.

steps.title: Coverslip IHC slides
steps.instruction: Mount the IHC slides after dehydration.

substeps.instruction: Coverslip the slides using Cytoseal XYL and a VWR 24 × 40 (or 24 × 50) coverglass.
Wipe the back of each slide and drain the sides to remove excess mounting media/xylene, then place the slides on a cardboard palette to dry overnight.
